newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Resources in HK$700 mln unit float - analysts.
newsitem.headline: China Resources in HK$700 mln unit float - analysts.

text.p: China Resources Enterprise Ltd plans to raise a total of HK$700 million by issuing 300 million new shares in its China property arm China Resources Beijing Land Ltd, analysts said on Friday.

"The group will place 85 percent of the issue internationally and the remaining 15 percent will open to public subscription on November 1, at the latest," said an analyst who attended an analysts' briefing on Thursday.
China Resources did not give a price range for the issue but a source close to the underwriters said the price would fall within a range of HK$1.99 and HK$2.36 per share.
China Resources was not immediately available for comment.
The preliminary listing document said a final price would be fixed on November 1 following the close of share placement on October 31, analysts said.
Dealing in the shares was expected to start on November 8.
"Its net asset value (NAV) is about HK$3.10 billion and China Resources is aiming for a price at around a 30 percent discount to the NAV," an analyst at a European house said.

The prospectus said the issue would represent about 25 percent of the company's enlarged share capital and the group also agreed to issue up to 45 million new shares separately to cover over-allotment, the analyst said.
Beijing Land's major asset was a 62.5 percent stake in Beijing Huayuan Properties Co, a local property developer and investor, analysts said.
They said Beijing Huayuan has a property portfolio of 2.6 million square metres, worth a total of HK$8.48 billion.
Thirty-nine percent of Beijing Huayuan's land bank was in the western part of Beijing and the remaining 61 percent in other parts of the city, another analyst said.

Analysts said the presentation document showed that about 47 percent of the total gross floor areas of the portfolio was residential properties, 12 percent for resettlement, 11 percent for supporting facilities, 17 percent for commercial usage with the remainder for other purposes.
The company posted a net profit of HK$181 million in calendar year 1995 and forecast a net profit of not less than HK$240 million in 1996, the company told the analysts.
